title: Geo-Fidelity Steering Optimizer: latency-aware pinning with capacity negotiation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Our current multi-region routing uses static geo pin thresholds and simple latency hedging. During cross-region surges we either over-pin (increasing latency for local users) or over-eject (excessive load shedding). This ticket proposes a Geo-Fidelity Steering Optimizer: a routing component that negotiates capacity budgets with the regional admission controller and applies soft pinning and probabilistic hedging to meet latency SLOs while minimizing cross-region cost and shedding.
acceptance_criteria: New steering component implemented behind feature flag that can negotiate per-region capacity budgets via the admission API
Latency P50/P95 for 95th percentile of routes is maintained within configured SLOs in canary region tests
End-to-end integration tests for pinning downgrade and soft-eviction scenarios pass in CI
System emits visibility metrics: negotiated_budget, effective_pin_fraction, shed_count_by_region, fallback_rate
Rollout plan documented with canary gating and automated rollback on SLO regressions
design_notes: Core idea: introduce a lightweight two-way negotiation protocol between Router and Regional Admission Controller (RAC). Router proposes pin_fraction and estimated token load; RAC responds with granted_budget and a backpressure score (0..1).
Soft pinning: instead of binary pin/unpin, maintain per-route pin_fraction in [0,1]. Router uses pin_fraction to probabilistically route local requests; reduces sharp capacity cliffs.
Capacity-aware hedging: hedging policy uses granted_budget and recent measured queueing latency to decide hedged replicas and timeout windows. Hedging aggressive when backpressure_score > 0.7.

Circuit breakers: implement token-level circuit breakers with three stages: observe -> probation -> open. Probation uses reduced concurrency and higher sampling for failure detection to avoid noisy ejections.

Load shedding: implement priority tiers with graceful partial shedding. Non-essential telemetry / low-priority customers receive higher shed probability under budget shortfalls; expose per-tenant budgets to the Router.
SLO mapping: each route declares target latency SLO and egress cost preference (low-cost vs low-latency). Router optimizes pin_fraction to satisfy latency SLO, subject to granted_budget constraints.
Fallback behavior: if negotiation fails or RAC is unreachable, fall back to configured regional default pin_fraction with a conservative fail-safe hedging multiplier.
Compatibility: API is implemented as extension of existing steering RPCs to avoid changes to downstream components; feature gated behind steering_v2 flag.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable steering_v2 in two internal test workspaces and one low-volume customer region for 48h
Phase 2 (regional staging): expand to three additional regions with synthetic load tests simulating 2x normal burst patterns
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 10% of global traffic routed via new optimizer, monitor SLOs for 24h, then 50% if stable
Phase 4 (full): global rollout with automated rollback on SLO or error-rate regressions
Safety net: automatic revert if p95 latency increases > 10% for 30 minutes or error_rate increases > 0.5% absolute
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: SLO-breach-alert if p95_latency(route_group) exceeds target for 15m and correlated with steering.change_events
Alert: RAC-unreachable if negotiation RPC fails > 1% of attempts over 5m
Dashboard: geo-fidelity dashboard combining regional capacity, pin fractions, hedging events, and shedding counts
Tracing: add spans around negotiation handshake and final routing decision to correlate latency regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for negotiation state machine and pin_fraction arithmetic
Integration tests: Router + RAC in docker-compose with injected latency and capacity limits
Chaos tests: simulated RAC flaps, stale budgets, and split-brain routing under network partition
Performance tests: end-to-end p95 measured under 5 concurrent burst profiles at 1k qps
E2E customer-facing test: run canary with synthetic customers that verify per-tenant SLOs and billing signals
open_questions: What default pin_fraction should be used when RAC denies negotiation? (proposal: 0.25 conservative)
How to expose per-tenant budget negotiation securely for Dedicated/private deployments without leaking capacity signals?
Should the negotiation protocol be rate-limited to avoid extra control-plane load during large global surges?
Do we need a global coordination tier for multi-region allocations or keep negotiation strictly pairwise (router <-> region)?
How to integrate this with existing autoscaler signals to avoid oscillation between steering adjustments and scale events?
